figures.caption: Fig. 4: Output-token usage by arm for each model (log-scaled axis for visualization only; all primary analyses are rank-based tests on untransformed token counts; lower is better). Panel annotations give paired Wilcoxon significance: *** p < 0.001, ** p < 0.01, * p < 0.05.
Fig. 5: Binary correctness by model and arm with 95% confidence intervals.

Fig. 1: Task-bank construction. The “library” generator composes a coherent program of K named analysis functions plus a driver, with K setting program length (tiers T2–T6); six standalone composite templates provide T1. Together they yield the 36 task instances of Table I.
Fig. 6: Mean partial-credit score by file-size tier and arm. The FileMark advantage emerges at T4 and both arms collapse for local models at T5–T6.

Fig. 8: The function-patch contract. The model receives the full seed and the feedback (both arms); it returns only the corrected functions, which the harness applies to the seed by name before validation.
Fig. 2: Scoring pipeline. Every run yields a three-level run status, a partial-credit score, and binary correctness; both arms pass through the identical pipeline.

Fig. 7: Run status by model, with control and treatment side by side within each category (error / runs-fail / correct). FileMark shrinks the silent runs_fail category for the coder-tuned local models.

Fig. 9: Run status by model under the exploratory function-patch contract (T4–T6 wave), with control and treatment side by side within each category. With the harness applying the edits, every local model’s correct share rises under FileMark.
Fig. 3: Experiment pipeline. Both arms are derived from the same changes.json, so only the feedback format differs between control and treatment.
